generalfeedback.text:
A table is a probability distribution when every probability is from 0 to 1 and the probabilities add up to exactly 1. Check both.

Table 1: the probabilities add to \([[if test="is(f1=1)"]]{@tot1@}[[else]]{@pdec(tot1)@}[[/if]]\). [[if test="is(cn1=1)"]]Every value is from 0 to 1, so it is a probability distribution.[[elif test="is(cn1=2)"]]That is not 1, so it is not a probability distribution.[[else]]They add to 1, but \([[if test="is(f1=1)"]]{@bd1@}[[else]]{@pdec(bd1)@}[[/if]]\) is [[if test="is(bd1<0)"]]negative[[else]]more than 1[[/if]], so it cannot be a probability: this is not a probability distribution.[[/if]]

Table 2: the probabilities add to \([[if test="is(f2=1)"]]{@tot2@}[[else]]{@pdec(tot2)@}[[/if]]\). [[if test="is(cn2=1)"]]Every value is from 0 to 1, so it is a probability distribution.[[elif test="is(cn2=2)"]]That is not 1, so it is not a probability distribution.[[else]]They add to 1, but \([[if test="is(f2=1)"]]{@bd2@}[[else]]{@pdec(bd2)@}[[/if]]\) is [[if test="is(bd2<0)"]]negative[[else]]more than 1[[/if]], so it cannot be a probability: this is not a probability distribution.[[/if]]

Table 3: the probabilities add to \([[if test="is(f3=1)"]]{@tot3@}[[else]]{@pdec(tot3)@}[[/if]]\). [[if test="is(cn3=1)"]]Every value is from 0 to 1, so it is a probability distribution.[[elif test="is(cn3=2)"]]That is not 1, so it is not a probability distribution.[[else]]They add to 1, but \([[if test="is(f3=1)"]]{@bd3@}[[else]]{@pdec(bd3)@}[[/if]]\) is [[if test="is(bd3<0)"]]negative[[else]]more than 1[[/if]], so it cannot be a probability: this is not a probability distribution.[[/if]]

questiondescription.text:
Probability III: recognising a probability distribution

Grade 12 CBE Essential 3.2: Decide whether a table is a probability distribution by checking the range of each value and the total.

Essential

This question is based on the text of Chapter 4, Section A of Cassell, D., Instone, S., Ling, J., Scruton, P., Shilton, S. and West, H., SMP AS/A2 Mathematics: Statistics 1 for AQA, Cambridge University Press, 2004: the two conditions on a probability distribution, turned into a three-way classification of curated tables.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Essential Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

truefeedback.text:
[[if test="is(cn1=1)"]]

Add them: the total is exactly 1.

[[elif test="is(cn1=2)"]]

Every value is from 0 to 1, but that is only one of the two conditions. What do the probabilities add up to?

[[else]]

Add them: the total is exactly 1. Now look at each value on its own: can every one be a probability?

[[/if]]

falsefeedback.text:
[[if test="is(cn1=1)"]]

Every value is from 0 to 1. A probability of 0 is allowed: that value can never happen.

[[elif test="is(cn1=2)"]]

Every value is between 0 and 1. Check the total.

[[else]]

The total is 1, but that is only one of the two conditions. Look at each value on its own: can every one be a probability?

[[/if]]
